name: Julie Ertz
notes: Plaintiff in the 2019 USWNT equal-pay lawsuit. Trophies: World Cups 2015, 2019 + CONCACAF titles 2014, 2018.

name: Julie Foudy
notes: Inspected Pakistani ball factories for child labour (1997 FIFA Fair Play Award); led 1995-96 pay holdout. Trophies: World Cups 1991, 1999 + 5 CONCACAF titles.

name: Julien Friedrich
notes: Union Berlin academy; loan at Altglienicke 2025-26.

name: Just Fontaine
notes: Co-founded and first president of the French players' union UNFP (1961) against lifetime contracts.

name: Kaká
notes: UN World Food Programme ambassador.

name: Karim Adeyemi
notes: 2025: penalty order (EUR 450k) for buying a prohibited weapon (knuckle-duster with taser) online; apologised; no criminal record entry.

name: Karim Benzema
notes: Convicted 2021 of complicity in the Valbuena sex-tape blackmail (1-year suspended); acquitted 2014 in underage prostitution case; Saudi clubs 2023-26 and Saudi league ambassador.

name: Karl-Heinz Rummenigge
notes: 2013: accepted a penalty order for tax evasion (~EUR 250k) over undeclared Rolex watches from Qatar.

name: Kelly Smith
notes: Spoke openly about alcoholism and depression; mental-health advocacy.

name: Kenny Dalglish
notes: Supported Hillsborough families; Marina Dalglish Appeal raised over GBP 13m for cancer care.

name: Kevin Keegan
notes: 1974 Charity Shield: traded punches with Billy Bremner, both sent off; FA ban and fine.

name: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia
notes: Refused Napoli renewal and pushed for a January 2025 move to PSG.

name: Kristine Lilly
notes: Part of the 1995-96 pay holdout. Trophies: World Cups 1991, 1999 + 6 CONCACAF titles.

name: Kyle Edwards
notes: Born 1997 (Wikipedia); St Vincent international (34 caps to Oct 2025); clubs from Wikipedia.

name: Kylian Mbappé
notes: Named by Swedish media in a 2024 Stockholm rape investigation closed for insufficient evidence (never notified as suspect); funds Premiers de Cordée; legal dispute with PSG over wages.

name: Lamine Yamal
notes: 2025 18th-birthday party controversy (Spain's equality ministry asked for investigation); no charge.

name: Landon Donovan
notes: As San Diego Loyal coach (2020) led two walk-offs over racist and homophobic slurs, forfeiting points. Trophies: 6 MLS Cups + 4 Gold Cups.

name: Lauren James
notes: 2023 World Cup: red card for stamping on Michelle Alozie, 2-match ban, apologised; spoke out about racist online abuse.

name: Leah Williamson
notes: Campaigned on white shorts and periods; LGBTQ allyship; public about endometriosis.

name: Lena Oberdorf
notes: Moved from Wolfsburg to direct title rival Bayern (2024).

name: Lindsey Horan
notes: Plaintiff in the 2019 USWNT equal-pay lawsuit.

name: Lionel Messi
notes: 2016 Spanish tax-fraud conviction (image rights; 21-month suspended, converted to fine); paid Visit Saudi ambassador since 2022; 2019 CONMEBOL ban for corruption claims; UNICEF ambassador and Leo Messi Foundation.

name: Lothar Matthäus
notes: 1984: agreed a direct move from Gladbach to title rival Bayern, then missed a penalty against Bayern in the cup final.

name: Lucy Bronze
notes: Advocacy on neurodiversity after disclosing autism and ADHD.

name: Luis Suárez
notes: Bit Bakkal (2010), Ivanović (2013), Chiellini (2014); spat at a Seattle staff member (2025); 8-match ban for racially abusing Evra (2011); pushed to leave Liverpool in 2013.

name: Luka Modrić
notes: Perjury charge in the Mamić trial dismissed; skipped Tottenham's 2012 pre-season tour to force his Real Madrid move.

name: Luís Figo
notes: 2000: moved from Barcelona to Real Madrid via release clause.

name: Manuel Neuer
notes: Wore rainbow armband at Euro 2020 (UEFA probe dropped) and backed the OneLove gesture at Qatar 2022; Manuel Neuer Kids Foundation; 2023 club fine for unauthorised interview.

name: Marcel Desailly
notes: Ex-partner's 2013 police record (main courante) alleging violence, reported in a paternity suit; no charge or ruling. Ended career in Qatar (Al-Gharafa, Qatar SC).

name: Marco Reus
notes: 2014: fined EUR 540,000 for driving for years without a licence.

name: Marco van Basten
notes: 2020: said 'Sieg Heil' on live Dutch TV; apologised, pay docked.

name: Marcus Rashford
notes: Free school meals campaign forced two UK government U-turns (2020). Jan 2024: fined and dropped after a night out.

name: Marta
notes: UN Women Goodwill Ambassador; refused boot deals without equal terms (2019).

name: Mary Earps
notes: 2023 campaign that made Nike sell her goalkeeper shirt.

name: Mats Hummels
notes: 2016: left as Dortmund captain for rival Bayern (returned 2019). First German player in Common Goal (1% of wages).

name: Matt Le Tissier
notes: Spread COVID vaccine misinformation (2021) and Bucha 'false flag' posts (2022); resigned as Southampton ambassador.

name: Matthias Sindelar
notes: 1938: bought a Jewish-owned café through Nazi 'Aryanisation' at a below-value price; his role and knowledge are disputed. Declined to play for Germany after the Anschluss.

name: Megan Rapinoe
notes: Lead voice in the USWNT equal-pay suit; knelt for the anthem in 2016 (booed, prompted a US Soccer rule); LGBTQ+ advocacy.
